KEY MESSAGE 1...Windy and warm today with a diminishing 
potential for showers and thunderstorms. 

A low pressure system moving through Ontario into Quebec today has 
currently deepened to around 990 mb. This low pressure system drags 
a cold front through the region into tonight. The trend this 
afternoon among model guidance has been a continued downward trend 
with shower and thunderstorm potential. Given the downward trend, 
most of the area is now in a MARGINAL risk with the southern portion 
of Delmarva being maintained at a SLIGHT risk. Even though the trend 
has been downward, the potential for showers and thunderstorms is 
not zero given the strong kinematics aloft, steep low-level lapse 
rates, and some instability being present. Any storm that does 
develop will be capable of producing damaging wind gusts. What has 
limited the potential for showers and thunderstorms developing today 
is the better forcing being off to the north along with lower 
instability due to the showers and cloud cover this morning. No 
changes to the general timeframe of any stronger to severe 
thunderstorm with that looking to remain to be through around 8 PM.

A bigger piece of the story today has been the gusty winds due to 
the tight pressure gradient across the region from the deepening low 
pressure system moving by to the north and a strong Bermuda high 
pressure system offshore. Winds have at times been gusting up to 40 
MPH.

The final storyline for today has been the one-day surge in 
temperatures. Due to the strong warm-air advection that has set up 
from the gusty southwesterly flow, highs today reach the upper 80s 
to low 90s. After the frontal passage tonight, more seasonable 
temperatures return for tomorrow with highs in the low 80s along 
with lower humidity values.

Depending on the placement of the front, some showers and perhaps an 
isolated thunderstorm is possible across portions of Delmarva and 
southern NJ tomorrow morning. As the front continues to sink south 
tomorrow, we trend dry across the area into the afternoon.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A High Risk for the development of rip cornets 
is in place for the Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches today.

A Rip Current Statement has been issued for today for the 
Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches

For today, south-southwest winds will be increasing to around 
15 to 25 mph with gusts as high as 25 to 35 mph in the 
afternoon. There will be a southeasterly 4 to 6 foot swell at 6 
to 7 seconds. Breaking wave heights of 3 to 5 feet expected as 
well. As a result, with strong winds in a shore parallel or 
offshore direction, and 3 to 5 foot breakers, elected for a HIGH
risk for the development of rip currents at all beaches. 

For Friday, west-southwesterly winds generally 5-15 mph. There 
will be a south-southeasterly swell of 3 to 5 feet at around 7 
seconds. Breaking wave heights of 1 to 3 feet are anticipated. 
Have opted for a MODERATE risk for the Jersey Shore and a LOW 
risk for Delaware beaches for the development of dangerous rip 
currents, where flow is more offshore. Did consider downgrading 
the Jersey Shore given tranquil conditions, but will have to see
how quickly windy and rough conditions in the surf zone taper 
off. 

For Saturday, westerly winds remain around 10-15 mph. However,
the onshore swells begin to weaken, decreasing to around 2 to 4
at around a 7 second period. Breaking waves in the surf zone
should be around 2 feet or less as a result. Therefore, a LOW
risk for the development of dangerous rip currents is forecast
for all beaches on Saturday.

For specific beach forecasts, visit weather.gov/beach/phi


KEY MESSAGE 3...Minor tidal flooding expected to occur with 
this afternoon's high tide along northern Barnegat Bay. Spotty 
minor tidal flooding is likely elsewhere within the backbays of 
Atlantic coastal Delaware and New Jersey.

Strong south to southwest winds are expected to bring a round of
minor tidal flooding to the northern shore of Barnegat Bay with
this afternoon's high tide. A Coastal Flood Advisory was issued
to highlight this threat, which is in effect until 8 PM. 
Elsewhere along the Atlantic coasts of Delaware and New Jersey, 
some spotty minor flooding may occur as well near today or 
tonight's high tide.

Beyond tonight, astronomical tides should be low enough to 
prevent any additional flooding impacts. We'll also have a
modest offshore wind through at least Saturday, which will help
drain the bays most substantially.
